The Federal Parliament building is stormed and set on fire by protesters.

Israel carries out a series of airstrikes against alleged Houthi targets and civilian structures in Sanaa and Al Jawf Governorate, Yemen, killing 35 people and wounding 131 others.
The Polish Air Force and NATO allies scramble fighter jets in response to 19 Russian drones penetrating up to 250 km into Polish airspace during an overnight air attack on Ukraine.
The Polish Armed Forces confirms it has shot down four Russian drones over the country, marking the first time Poland has directly engaged Russian military assets since the start of the war.
Poland closes multiple airports due to the airspace breach, including Warsaw Modlin Airport, Rzeszów–Jasionka Airport, and Lublin Airport.
Polish prime minister Donald Tusk invokes Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty following the incursion.

11.title: The casualty toll from yesterday's Israeli airstrikes in Sanaa and Al Jawf Governorate, Yemen, increases to 46 people killed and 165 others injured.
At least nine people are killed when a lifeboat carrying flood evacuees capsizes near Multan, Punjab, Pakistan, while 15 others are safely rescued.

At least 107 people are killed and 146 remain missing after a whaleboat catches fire on the Congo River near Lukolela, Équateur Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with over 200 survivors rescued.
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo doubles in cases as the virus spreads to more districts in Kasai province.
Clean energy think tank Ember reports that wind and solar power generated over one-third of Brazil's electricity for the first time in August.
Belarus releases 52 political prisoners, including 14 foreign nationals, following negotiations with the United States.

12.title: A Palestinian assailant stabs two Israeli civilians in Tzova, Jerusalem District.

At least 42 people are killed by armed gangs, including the Viv Ansamn, in Port-au-Prince, Haiti.
At least 18 people, mostly students, are killed in a Tatmadaw airstrike on two schools in Kyauktaw Township in Rakhine State, Myanmar, an area controlled by the Arakan Army.

Turkish police arrest 161 people suspected of being members of the Islamic State (IS) over the last week and seize unlicensed weapons and IS documents in raids in 38 provinces, including Istanbul and Ankara.

Norges Bank removes French mining company Eramet from Norway's sovereign wealth fund, citing risks of human rights abuses and environmental damage linked to a nickel mining project in Halmahera, Indonesia.

At least 19 people are killed after a bus carrying wedding guests plunged into a river in Zamfara State, Nigeria.
At least 15 people are killed in a multi-vehicle collision along Federal Highway 180 between Campeche and Mérida in southeast Mexico.

At the 2025 Primetime Emmy Awards in the United States, The Studio becomes the most-nominated first-year comedy series in the awards' history at 23 nominations, tying The Bear's nominations from last year.
For the first time in the awards' history, every nominee for Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series has at least one woman on the writing team.
The Studio wins Outstanding Comedy Series and The Pitt wins Outstanding Drama Series, while Adolescence wins Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series.

At least 100 people are feared dead following the collapse of a gold mining pit in Zamfara State, Nigeria.

Puerto Rican artist Bad Bunny is announced as the headliner for Super Bowl LX to be held on February 8, 2026, at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, United States.
At least thirteen people are killed and dozens others are missing as Typhoon Bualoi makes landfall in Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh provinces, Vietnam.
Twelve people are killed and 42 injured in three separate road accidents in Panjgur, Pishin and Lasbela, Pakistan.

German airline Lufthansa announces they will cut 4,000 administrative positions by 2030 and replace them with artificial intelligence and digitization processes.

30.title: At least 59 Palestinians are killed by Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip, including 20 who were seeking aid.
A Palestinian man rams into Israeli pedestrians near Al-Khader in the West Bank, injuring two children, before being shot.

An overnight Russian drone strike kills four people, all members of the same family, in Chernechchyna, Okhtyrka Raion, Sumy Oblast, Ukraine.
Two-year-old Aryatara Shakya is installed in Kathmandu as Nepal's new Kumari, succeeding Trishna Shakya who held the role since 2017.
A Mw 6.9 earthquake hits the central Philippines with structural damage and power interruptions reported, particularly in Cebu where at least 69 people are reported dead.
